key_insight: A simple constraint-aware server aggregation rule in federated reinforcement learning can improve both reward and safety by penalizing estimated constraint violations during model averaging.
engineering_relevance: For microgrid coordination, this offers a lightweight way to reduce unsafe dispatch behavior without changing local training or communication protocols.
method: Aggregate client updates with weights proportional to reward minus a violation penalty, w_i ∝ R_i − αV_i.
Compare against standard FedAvg and a combined reward-violation scheme with a tunable trade-off λ.
Evaluate on distributed battery coordination under a shared grid-capacity constraint, including real load-driven demand profiles.
evidence_signal: Across multiple seeds on DairyGridEnv and real load profiles from Finland and the German FIELD dataset, penalty-based aggregation reduced constraint violations and improved reward relative to FedAvg.
watch_item: The trade-off depends on penalty tuning, and the combined reward-violation variant was less stable, so deployment may require careful calibration.
paper_title: Constraint-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Microgrid Energy Coordination
